script: Am I the jerk for hiding my dead dog's bowls and refusing to go to Spain for my mum's anniversary with my dad's new girlfriend?. I recently lost my mom. Her death hit me like a ton of bricks, and I've been drowning in grief. But here's the thing—my dad's already moving on. He's got this woman, AM, who he says he's known for 40 years. She shows up almost daily, and the first time I saw her was after Mom's funeral. What I didn't know was that she only started visiting when Mom was gone. My dad swears there's no drama, but he bought AM an iPhone for her birthday. And now she's moving in because her landlord kicked her out. Until now I thought it was temporary, but I just found out he's actually looking to buy a house with her. If this didn't work, I'd lose my sanity and my sense of home. The stakes are high—this isn't just about money or space; it's about my mental health. And that's when everything changed. AM brought her crusty white dog, Rosy. Rosy's a total menace: no training, no personal space, pees and poos all over the kitchen. Being autistic, I am always on high alert, masking in my own house just to get a snack. But here's the thing—Rosy's chaos is like a constant sensory assault. The breaking point came when my beloved dog, Bruno, passed away. He had accidents in his last days, and my dad would scream and say he was "glad" Bruno died. Honestly, that was the most hurtful thing anyone said. And that's when everything changed. Now, AM forces Rosy to use Bruno's old bowls. She's not even bringing bowls, so she's just using what's left. The audacity of using Bruno's stuff while telling me I am glad he died made me so furious I took those bowls, washed them, and hid them in my room. But here's the thing—my dad thinks I am petty for doing that. My brother won't back me up because he's dating AM's daughter, C. C's over all the time, so my brother keeps quiet, not wanting to stir up drama. It feels like everyone's against me, but for them, it's fine to have a friend 24/7. What I didn't know was that I'd be the odd one out. AM is trying way too hard to get on my good side. She lent me some books, which was fine, but then she offered to take me bra shopping. No? That's a total boundary crossing. And that's when everything changed. She also told my dad to buy me a horse if they move houses just because I like them. That felt manipulative and fake, like a game she's playing. I am like, "I am not a toy, AM." But here's the thing—my dad is still in the dark about how much I am hurting. My mom's one-year death anniversary is coming. I want a quiet, private time to grieve with family. Instead, my dad wants to take us to Spain, and he's bringing AM and C along. I asked to bring a friend for support, and he said no, because he invited AM's other daughter, N, who I haven't seen since I was five. What I didn't know was that he'd give me an ultimatum: "You can stay at home then, and we'll go." I am staying home. I refuse to go to Spain and pretend to be a happy blended family on my mom's anniversary while I am on sensory burnout. My dad and brother think I am stubborn, selfish, and an asshole. But here's the thing—my brain is on fire, and I can't keep pretending. I am not the jerk; I am the only one who can't stand the chaos. And that's when everything changed—my dad's silence, AM's manipulations, and Rosy's mess all built up to this point. Now the big question: will my dad listen, or will AM's influence keep pulling me into a family I don't want? I don't know what to do next, but I feel like I am on the edge of something huge. And then, just as I was about to decide, the phone buzzed—an unknown number, a message that said, "Let's talk." (Will I answer? The cliffhanger hangs, and I am left staring at the screen, heart racing.)
